heroHeadline: FIFA Counterattacks: Infantino's Federation Accuses UEFA of 'Smear Campaign' in US Court Filing
heroSubtitle: Seven weeks after Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time to win the World Cup Final at MetLife Stadium (July 19), FIFA moved from defense to offense in its dispute with UEFA over Gianni Infantino's abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan. FIFA filed a motion Sep 3 in Colorado federal court seeking to block or defer UEFA's discovery requests — filed in three US courts, including one targeting Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital — that UEFA is pursuing to build a Swiss criminal complaint against Infantino for 'criminal mismanagement.' FIFA's filing called the requests 'little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership,' arguing UEFA lacks legal standing since no Swiss criminal proceedings yet exist; FIFA repeated the accusation again Sep 4. The legal counterpunch came days after the Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB), one of FIFA's seven founding members, said Aug 30 it had lost confidence in Infantino and, unlike most federations demanding only his exit, called for power to shift from the presidency to FIFA's secretary-general and proposed an international reform summit in Amsterdam ahead of the March 18, 2027 election in Rabat. That followed Italy's football federation (FIGC) withdrawing support for his re-election bid (Aug 26), and court filings in Manhattan and southern Florida revealing UEFA's original criminal-complaint preparations under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code (Aug 27).
